title: ExamLeaf scene cue sheet
description: One canonical cue sheet per scene (research report section 5.5). All times are in seconds from scene start. Scene code reads cues[].at and never hard-codes times. If narration is regenerated: re-align, rebuild this file, re-render; scene code does not change. Structural rules are enforced by validate_cue_sheet.py, which reads this file; semantic rules (monotonic times, non-overlapping words, cues within duration) are enforced by that script because JSON Schema draft-07 cannot express them.

schema_version.description: Cue sheet format version. Independent of the contract version; see contract.md section 14.

scene_id.description: Stable scene identifier, for example phy-10-03-s04.

fps.description: Intended render fps. Times are in seconds and are authoritative; if the renderer uses a different fps the renderer's fps wins and a warning is logged.

duration.description: Scene duration in seconds. Becomes window.DURATION. Frame count = round(duration * fps). Derived from the narration, not the other way round.

language.description: Primary narration language, BCP-47 style (hi-IN, as-IN, en-IN). Code-switched words carry their own lang.

alignment_source.description: How word times were produced. synthetic_even_spacing and example are NOT valid for production (validate_cue_sheet.py --production rejects them).

narration_audio_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the narration audio file these times were aligned to. null only while no narration exists (validator --production rejects null).

script_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the approved script text. The animation agent never edits approved text; a changed hash means re-approval and re-alignment.

words.description: Word timings in spoken order. t0 is when the word starts, t1 when it ends. Words must not overlap.

beats.description: Beat times in seconds (librosa units='time', never frames). Strictly increasing. Empty is allowed: silent or beatless audio gives an empty list [N41]; fall back to the narration grid.

meta.description: Free-form provenance (tool names, notes). Not restricted by this schema. Optional documented fields (16 Oct 2026, pilot gaps L-03/L-05), which scene code MAY read: meta.beats_text[] = {id, slot, text (verbatim script text, punctuation intact; words[] strips punctuation), headline, start, end, word_range} per script beat, times in scene-local seconds; meta.think_windows[] = {beat, seconds, start, end} for each predict pause, so a scene knows when its Pause/Predict plate shows. Scene boundaries sit on the frame grid: the builder snaps each scene start to a whole frame and scene-local time (words[].t0, cues[].at, these fields) starts at the snapped scene start.

w.description: The word as spoken and shown, in its own script (Devanagari, Bengali-Assamese or Latin).

occurrence.description: 1-based index of this surface form among identical words in the scene. Lets a cue refer to 'the second occurrence'.

lang.description: Language of this word when it differs from the sheet language (code-switching).

at.description: Cue time in seconds. For a reveal keyed to a word: at <= word.t0 and at >= word.t0 - 0.05 (the 'on or 0.05 s before' rule).

element_id.description: DOM or scene element this cue drives.

occurrence.description: 1-based index when the same id fires more than once (repeat emphasis). Omit for a single firing.

word_index.description: Index into words[] that this cue is keyed to. Enables the reveal-lead check.

until.description: End time for kind=hold (for example narration end + 0.5 s for an equation).

file.description: Relative path to a 48 kHz WAV or FLAC one-shot. No absolute paths, no '..' segments (validator rejects).

gain_db.description: Attenuation relative to the library master level. Positive gain is not allowed (clipping).
